takeaway.old: Explains how enforcement is shared from 2 August 2026 between the AI Office, the EDPS for Union institutions and national market surveillance authorities. The AI Office supervises GPAI models and, after the Omnibus, systems built on them and AI in very large online platforms, using information requests, model evaluations, interviews and inspections. Penalty ceilings are EUR 35 million or 7 percent of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices, EUR 15 million or 3 percent for GPAI and other operator breaches, and EUR 7.5 million or 1 percent for misleading information. The deepfake and CSAM bans apply from 2 December 2026.

takeaway.old: Article 64(2) GDPR opinion adopted 17 December 2024 and published the next day, at the request of the Irish supervisory authority. It holds that an AI model trained on personal data is anonymous only where the likelihood of extracting individuals' data from the model or obtaining it through queries is insignificant, assessed case by case; sets a three-step test for legitimate interest in training and deployment, with conversational agents and threat detection as acceptable purposes when strictly necessary and balanced; and warns that models built on unlawfully processed data may face corrective measures and restrictions on subsequent use unless properly anonymised. It does not implement the AI Act but governs the data side that Article 2(7) leaves to the GDPR.
takeaway.new: Article 64(2) GDPR opinion adopted 17 December 2024 and published the next day, at the request of the Irish supervisory authority. Not binding, but it is the Board's settled position on AI models under the GDPR. It holds that an AI model trained on personal data is anonymous only where the likelihood of extracting individuals' data from the model or obtaining it through queries is insignificant, assessed case by case; sets a three-step test for legitimate interest in training and deployment, with conversational agents and threat detection as acceptable purposes when strictly necessary and balanced; and warns that models built on unlawfully processed data may face corrective measures and restrictions on subsequent use unless properly anonymised. It does not implement the AI Act but governs the data side that Article 2(7) leaves to the GDPR.
